findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: entire program aborts on disk/file errors instead of returning a typed I/O error to the caller
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain I/O error type) and propagate fs::read_to_string with ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric field values
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input (e.g., alpha text in the value column) causes a panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: replace .unwrap() with map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e.to_string())) or an equivalent typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing; no validation that split produced at least 2 fields
findings.failure_mode: a CSV line with fewer than 2 commas (e.g., a blank line or single-word line) causes a bounds panic via Index::index
findings.fix: check parts.len() >= 2 before indexing, or use split_once(',') and pattern-match the pair

findings.problem: lossy as u16 cast after parse::<u32>() - values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to 16 bits
findings.failure_mode: a sensor reading of 70000 becomes 4446 with no error or warning, corrupting sensor data downstream
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::OutOfRange) instead of as u16

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds side-effecting I/O (stdout logging) inside the data-loading / domain-construction path
findings.failure_mode: the pure parsing logic is polluted with hidden I/O, making the function untestable without capturing stdout and violating the Data/Calculations/Actions architecture
findings.fix: remove println! from the parsing closure; move all logging to an imperative shell layer that consumes the parsed records

findings.problem: load_sensors fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/collect), domain construction (Record), logging (println!), and collection (collect) in a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell: callers cannot reuse the parser without paying for file access, and the shell cannot customize error handling or logging strategy for the pure parsing step
findings.fix: split into (a) pure parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and (b) load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that handles I/O and delegates to parse_line

findings.problem: Record uses raw primitives (String, u16) with no domain invariants encoded in the type system
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct Record { name: String::new(), value: u16::MAX } or any invalid state; invalid states are not representable-by-construction
findings.fix: introduce a private module with a smart constructor Record::try_new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Record, RecordError> that validates constraints (non-empty name, value range)

findings.problem: no capacity cap or try_reserve on the intermediate Vec<String> per line and the final Vec<Record>; unbounded allocation from adversarial input
findings.failure_mode: a single extremely long CSV line can allocate megabytes for split parts; the final collect() has no upper bound, enabling denial-of-service via memory exhaustion
findings.fix: apply a domain cap on max_records before the outer collect, use try_reserve on both the intermediate Vec and the final Vec, and cap line length before splitting

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the load_sensors hot path
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, or similar) for the allocation profile of this function
no allocation audit (e.g., --emit=mir or custom allocator instrumentation) for intermediate Vec<String> and Vec<Record> materialization
no second-ring evidence (assembly, bounds-check removal) for any claimed zero-cost or allocation-free guarantees
no command evidence: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, or cargo test were not run; strict lint gate not verified
no command-truth evidence (CLI invocation logs or captured outputs) for any stated performance or correctness claims
residual_risk: Static review identified 8 BLOCKER findings covering panic surfaces (unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast), hidden I/O in pure parsing logic, shell leakage fusing I/O/parsing/domain construction, raw-primitive domain types, and unbounded allocation. No commands were executed and no benchmarks were run. The crate will panic on any malformed input, silently truncate out-of-range values, and lacks typed error propagation. All findings require source repair before any delivery gate can pass.
